- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect market resilience.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1.5x the spike peak or use moving average to smooth.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days or use 3-day rolling mean.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops after peak), model often holds high for 3+ days; apply downward bias of 2–5% per day post-peak.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent trends; use 14-day EMA or sentiment-weighted average to anchor forecast.
